This female Long-tailed Duck showed up at the Inks Dam Fish Hatchery about Christmas, 2013, and is still there. It has become accustomed to people such as the workers at the hatchery and is quite confiding to photographers. This morning I sat on the side of a small pond with a 500mm lens and 1.4X converter and took hundreds of images in gorgeous light. A special treat for central Texas....we only get these guys here for a visit occasionally. The bird uses several of the ponds in this hatchery complex.

description:
Long-tailed Duck
•	Trophic level: mainly secondary consumer
•	Description: A winter visitor from the Arctic. Females are unassuming in plumage and easy to mistake for other winter ducks from a distance, but males are quite striking with the signature cowlick-like tail, sleek black and white plumage, pink bill stripe, and headphone-like dark plumage beneath the eyes. Males also make a distinctly bizarre honking call when courting females. 
•	Life Cycle: 6 to 8 eggs incubated by the female for a month. Young, like many ducks, feed themselves but follow their mother around. Breed in the Arctic and winter along the coasts on either side of the northern portion of North America.
•	Stage: Adult, based on time and appearance
•	Sex: Both males and females are pictured. 
•	Habitat: The ocean or large lakes, often far from the shore. During breeding, tundra pools and lakes.
•	Predator: Arctic Fox
•	Prey: Mollusks like the Atlantic Ribbed Mussel
•	Competitor: Common Eider
